canonical_question: Is the Archimedes density calculation sensitive enough to detect porosity levels below 0.1%, which could significantly influence the high-temperature mechanical properties?

question_variants.question: Is the Archimedes density calculation sensitive enough to detect porosity levels below 0.1%, which could significantly influence the high-temperature mechanical properties?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The paper mentions density calculation via Archimedes' principle but does not specify the instrument resolution, sensitivity, or the lowest detectable porosity threshold (e.g., below 0.1%).

answers.answer: The text confirms the density was calculated by Archimedes' principle but does not report the sensitivity or the minimum detectable porosity level.
answers.measurement_outcome: Density calculated (value not specified in span)
answers.boundary_limitation: No sensitivity limits or detection threshold reported.
evidence_spans: SLM-built HEA had a face-centered cubic (FCC) single-phase random solid solution.
In addition, SLM-built HEA was composed of epitaxial growth grains, dislocation network and nano-sized oxides.

Room- and high-temperature compression tests confirmed that SLM-built HEA has outstanding mechanical properties in all temperature ranges compared to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEAs reported up to the present.
